segments.arabic:
١١٤٠٧- صفية بنت حيّي
بن أخطب بن سعنة بن ثعلبة بن عبيد بن كعب «١» بن أبي حبيب، من بني النضير، وهو من سبط لاوى بن يعقوب، ثم من ذرية هارون بن عمران أخي موسى ﵉.
كانت تحت سلام بن مشكم، ثم خلف عليها كنانة بن أبي الحقيق، فقتل كنانة يوم خيبر، فصارت صفية مع السبي، فأخذها دحية ثم استعادها النبيّ ﷺ فأعتقها وتزوجها. ثبت ذلك في الصحيحين من حديث أنس مطولا ومختصرا.
وقال ابن إسحاق في رواية يونس بن بكير، عنه: حدثني والدي إسحاق بن يسار، قال: لما فتح رسول اللَّه ﷺ الغموص حصن بني أبي الحقيق أتى بصفية بنت حيي ومعها ابنة عم لها جاء بهما بلال، فمرّ بهما على قتلى يهود، فلما رأتهم المرأة التي مع صفية صكّت وجهها، وصاحت وحثت التراب على وجهها فقال رسول اللَّه ﷺ: «أغربوا هذه الشّيطانة عنّي» «٢» . وأمر بصفية فجعلت خلفه وغطّى عليها ثوبه، فعرف الناس أنه اصطفاها لنفسه، وقال لبلال: «أنزعت الرّحمة من قبلك حين تمرّ بالمرأتين على قتلاهما» . وكانت صفية رأت قبل ذلك أنّ القمر وقع في حجرها، فذكرت ذلك لأمّها، فلطمت وجهها، وقالت: إنك لتمدّين عنقك إلى أن تكوني عند ملك العرب، فلم يزل الأثر في وجهها حتى أتى بها رسول اللَّه ﷺ، فسألها عنه، فأخبرته.
وأخرج ابن سعد عن الواقديّ بأسانيد له في قصة خيبر، قال: ولم يخرج من خيبر حتى طهرت صفية من حيضها فحملها وراءه، فلما صار إلى منزل على ستة أميال من خيبر مال يريد أن يعرّس بها فأبت عليه فوجد في نفسه، فلما كان بالصهباء وهي على بريد من خيبر نزل بها هناك فمشطتها أمّ سليم وعطرتها، قالت أم سنان الأسلمية: وكانت من أضوأ ما يكون من النساء، فدخل على أهله، فلما أصبح سألتها عما قال لها. فقالت: قال لي «ما حملك على الامتناع من النّزول أوّلا؟» فقلت. خشيت عليك من قرب اليهود، فزادها ذلك عنده.
(١) أسد الغابة ت (٧٠٦٣)، الاستيعاب: ت (٣٤٥٢) .
(٢) ذكره البغوي في التفسير ٦/ ٢٠٠.
segments.english:
11407—Safiyya bint Huyayy
ibn Akhtab ibn Sa'na ibn Tha'laba ibn Ubayd ibn Ka'b [1] ibn Abi Habib, of Banu al-Nadir. He was of the tribe of Levi ibn Jacob, and then of the descendants of Aaron ibn Imran, the brother of Moses—peace be upon him.

She was married to Sallam ibn Mishkam; then Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq married her after him. Kinana was killed on the day of Khaybar, and Safiyya became one of the captives. Dihya took her, but the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—then reclaimed her, emancipated her, and married her. This is established in the Two Sahihs through the hadith of Anas, in both lengthy and abridged versions.

Ibn Ishaq said, in Yunus ibn Bukayr's transmission from him: My father, Ishaq ibn Yasar, related to me, saying: When the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—conquered al-Ghamus, the fortress of Banu Abi al-Huqayq, Safiyya bint Huyayy was brought to him together with a paternal cousin of hers; Bilal had brought them both. He took them past the slain Jews. When the woman accompanying Safiyya saw them, she struck her face, screamed, and threw dust upon her face. The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said, “Take this she-devil away from me.” [2] He ordered that Safiyya be placed behind him and covered her with his garment, so the people knew that he had selected her for himself. He said to Bilal, “Has mercy been taken from you, that you should take the two women past their slain men?”

Before that, Safiyya had seen the moon fall into her lap. She mentioned this to her mother, who slapped her on the face and said, “You are surely craning your neck to be with the king of the Arabs.” The mark remained on her face until she was brought to the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He asked her about it, and she told him.

Ibn Sa'd related from al-Waqidi, through chains of transmission of his, in the account of Khaybar. He said: The Prophet did not depart Khaybar until Safiyya had become ritually pure after her menstruation, and he had her ride behind him. When he reached a stopping place six miles from Khaybar, he turned aside, intending to consummate the marriage with her, but she refused him, and he felt displeased. When he reached al-Sahba', which is one barid from Khaybar, he stopped there with her. Umm Sulaym combed her hair and perfumed her. Umm Sinan al-Aslamiyya said: “She was among the most radiant of women. He then went in to his wife. When morning came, I asked her what he had said to her. She replied, ‘He said to me, “What caused you to refuse to dismount at first?” I said, “I feared for you because the Jews were nearby.”’” This increased her standing with him.

[1] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7063; al-Isti'ab, entry 3452.

[2] Mentioned by al-Baghawi in his Tafsir, 6/200.

segments.arabic:
وقال ابن سعد أيضا: أخبرنا عفان، حدثنا حماد، عن ثابت، عن سمية، عن عائشة- أن رسول اللَّه ﷺ كان في سفر فاعتلّ بعير لصفية، وفي إبل زينب بنت جحش فضل، فقال لها: «إنّ بعيرا لصفيّة اعتلّ، فلو أعطيتها بعيرا» . فقالت: أنا أعطي تلك اليهودية! فتركها رسول اللَّه ﷺ ذا الحجة والمحرم شهرين أو ثلاثة لا يأتيها. قالت زينب: حتى يئست منه.
وأخرج ابن أبي عاصم، من طريق القاسم بن عوف، عن أبي برزة، قال: لما نزل النبيّ ﷺ خيبر كانت صفية عروسا في مجاسدها «١»، فرأت في المنام أنّ الشمس نزلت حتى وقعت على صدرها، فقصّت ذلك على زوجها، فقال: ما تمنّين إلا هذا الملك الّذي نزل بنا. قال: فافتتحها رسول اللَّه ﷺ، فضرب عنق زوجها صبرا ... الحديث. وفيه: فألقى تمرا على سقيفة، فقال: «كلوا من وليمة رسول اللَّه ﷺ على صفيّة» .
وذكر ابن سعد من طريق عطاء بن يسار، قال: لما قدمت صفية من خيبر أنزلت في بيت لحارثة بن النعمان فسمع نساء الأنصار فجئن ينظرن إلى جمالها، وجاءت عائشة متنقّبة، فلما خرجت خرج النبيّ ﷺ على أثرها، فقال: «كيف رأيت يا عائشة؟» قالت:
رأيت يهودية. فقال: «لا تقولي ذلك، فإنّها أسلمت وحسن إسلامها» ..
ولها ذكر في ترجمة أم سنان الأسلمية، وفي ترجمة أمية بنت أبي قيس.
وأخرج من طريق عبد اللَّه بن عمر العمري، قال: لما اجتلى رسول اللَّه ﷺ صفية رأى عائشة منتقبة بين النساء، فعرفها، فأدركها فأخذ بثوبها، فقال: «كيف رأيت يا شقيراء؟» .
وأخرج بسند صحيح من مرسل سعيد بن المسيّب، فقال: قدمت صفية وفي أذنها خوصة من ذهب، فوهبت منه لفاطمة ولنساء معها.
وأخرج التّرمذيّ من طريق كنانة مولى صفية أنها حدّثته، قالت: دخل عليّ النبيّ ﷺ وقد بلغني عن عائشة وحفصة كلام فذكرت له ذلك. فقال: «ألا قلت: وكيف تكونان خيرا منّي وزوجي محمّد وأبي هارون وعمّي موسى» . وكان بلغها أنهما قالتا: نحن أكرم على رسول اللَّه ﷺ منها، نحن أزواجه وبنات عمه.
وقال أبو عمر: كانت صفية عاقلة حليمة فاضلة، روينا أن جارية لها أتت عمر فقالت:
إن صفية تحبّ السبت وتصل اليهود، فبعث إليها فسألها عن ذلك، فقالت: أما السبت فإنّي
(١) قال ابن الأثير: هو جمع مجسد- بضم الميم- وهو المصبوغ المشبع بالجسد وهو الزّعفران والعصفر، والجسد والجساد: الزعفران أو نحوه من الصّبغ، وثوب مجسد ومجسّد: مصبوغ بالزعفران وقيل: هو الأحمر والمجسّد: ما أشبع صبغه من الثياب والجمع مجاسد. اللسان ١/ ٦٢٢.
segments.english:
Ibn Sa'd also said: Affan informed us: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Sumayya, from Aisha, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was on a journey when a camel belonging to Safiyya became ill. Zaynab bint Jahsh had spare camels, so he said to her, “A camel belonging to Safiyya has become ill; would that you give her a camel.” She said, “Am I to give one to that Jewish woman!” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, therefore stayed away from her during Dhu al-Hijja and al-Muharram—two or three months—without coming to her. Zaynab said, “Until I despaired of him.”

Ibn Abi Asim reported, by way of al-Qasim ibn Awf, from Abu Barza, who said: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, encamped at Khaybar, Safiyya was a bride in her dyed bridal garments.(1) In a dream she saw the sun descend until it fell upon her breast. She related this to her husband, who said, “You desire none other than this king who has encamped among us.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, conquered it and had her husband’s neck struck while he was held captive … the hadith. It also contains: He cast dates upon a roofed platform and said, “Eat from the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for Safiyya.”

Ibn Sa'd mentioned, by way of Ata ibn Yasar, who said: When Safiyya arrived from Khaybar, she was lodged in a house belonging to Haritha ibn al-Nu'man. The women of the Ansar heard of her and came to look at her beauty. Aisha came veiled, and when she departed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out after her and said, “What did you think, Aisha?” She replied, “I saw a Jewish woman.” He said, “Do not say that, for she has embraced Islam, and her Islam is good.”

She is also mentioned in the biographical notice of Umm Sinan al-Aslamiyya and in that of Umayya bint Abi Qays.

He reported by way of Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Umari, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, viewed Safiyya unveiled as a bride, he saw Aisha veiled among the women and recognized her. He caught up with her, took hold of her garment, and said, “What did you think, little ruddy one?”

He reported with a sound chain, as a mursal report from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Safiyya arrived wearing in her ear a gold ornament, and she gave some of it to Fatima and to women who were with her.

al-Tirmidhi reported by way of Kinana, the client of Safiyya, that she related to him: “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered upon me after some words spoken by Aisha and Hafsa had reached me, and I mentioned this to him. He said, ‘Why did you not say: How can you two be better than I, when my husband is Muhammad, my father is Aaron, and my paternal uncle is Moses?’” It had reached her that the two of them had said, “We are more honored in the sight of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, than she is: we are his wives and the daughters of his paternal uncle.”

Abu Umar said: Safiyya was intelligent, forbearing, and virtuous. We have transmitted that a slave girl of hers came to Umar and said, “Safiyya loves the Sabbath and maintains ties with the Jews.” He sent for Safiyya and questioned her about that. She replied, “As for the Sabbath, I—”

(1) Ibn al-Athir said: It is the plural of mujsad—with the letter mim bearing a damma—which is something dyed and saturated with jasad, namely saffron and safflower. al-jasad and al-jisad mean saffron or a similar dye. A garment described as mujsad or mujassad is dyed with saffron. It is also said to mean red. A mujassad garment is one thoroughly saturated with dye, and its plural is majasid. al-Lisan, 1/622.

segments.arabic:
لم أحبه منذ أبدلني اللَّه به الجمعة، وأما اليهود فإن لي فيهم رحما، فأنا أصلها، ثم قالت للجارية: ما حملك على هذا؟ قالت: الشيطان. قالت: اذهبي، فأنت حرة.
وأخرج ابن سعد بسند حسن، عن زيد بن أسلم، قال: اجتمع نساء النبي ﷺ في مرضه الّذي توفي فيه، واجتمع إليه نساؤه، فقالت صفية بنت حيّي: إني واللَّه يا نبيّ اللَّه لوددت أن الّذي بك بي، فغمزن أزواجه ببصرهن. فقال: مضمضن. فقلن: من أي شيء؟
فقال: من تغامزكنّ بها، واللَّه إنها لصادقة.
روت صفية عن النبي ﷺ، وروى عنها ابن أخيها ومولاها كنانة ومولاها الآخر يزيد بن معتب، وزين العابدين علي بن الحسين، وإسحاق بن عبد اللَّه بن الحارث بن مسلم بن صفوان.
قيل: ماتت سنة ست وثلاثين، حكاه ابن حبان، وجزم به ابن مندة، وهو غلط، فإنه علي بن الحسين لم يكن ولد، وقد ثبت سماعه منها في الصحيحين.
وقال الواقدي: ماتت سنة خمسين، وهذا أقرب.
وقد أخرج ابن سعد من حديث أمية بنت أبي قيس الغفارية بسند فيه الواقدي قالت:
أنا إحدى النسوة اللاتي زففن صفية إلى رسول اللَّه ﷺ، فسمعتها تقول: ما بلغت سبع عشرة سنة يوم دخلت على رسول اللَّه ﷺ. قال: وتوفيت صفية سنة اثنتين وخمسين في خلافة معاوية.
وأخرج ابن سعد أيضا بسند حسن عن كنانة مولى صفية، قال: قدمت بصفية بغلة لتردّ عن عثمان، فلقينا الأشتر فضرب وجه البغلة، فقالت: ردّوني لا يفضحني. قال: ثم وضعت حسنا بين منزلها ومنزل عثمان، فكانت تنقل إليه الطعام والماء.
segments.english:
“I have not loved it since Allah replaced it for me with Friday. As for the Jews, I have a bond of kinship among them, and I maintain it.” Then she said to the slave-girl, “What prompted you to do this?” She replied, “Satan.” Safiyya said, “Go, for you are free.”

Ibn Sa'd transmitted with a hasan chain from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The women of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—assembled during the illness in which he died, and his wives gathered around him. Safiyya bint Huyayy said, “By Allah, O Prophet of Allah, I wish that what is afflicting you were afflicting me.” His wives gestured at her with their eyes. He said, “Rinse out your mouths.” They asked, “On account of what?” He said, “On account of your winking at one another about her. By Allah, she is indeed telling the truth.”

Safiyya narrated from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Those who narrated from her were her nephew; her client Kinanah; her other client, Yazid ibn Mu'attib; Zayn al-'Abidin 'Ali ibn al-Husayn; and Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Muslim ibn Safwan.

It is said that she died in the year thirty-six. Ibn Hibban related this, and Ibn Mandah stated it categorically. This is an error, for 'Ali ibn al-Husayn had not yet been born then, whereas it is established in the two Sahih collections that he heard from her.

Al-Waqidi said that she died in the year fifty, and this is more likely.

Ibn Sa'd transmitted from the report of Umayya bint Abi Qays al-Ghifariyya, through a chain containing al-Waqidi; she said: “I was one of the women who conducted Safiyya as a bride to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I heard her say, ‘I had not reached seventeen years of age on the day I entered upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.’” He said: Safiyya died in the year fifty-two, during the caliphate of Mu'awiya.

Ibn Sa'd also transmitted with a hasan chain from Kinanah, the client of Safiyya, who said: “Safiyya came on a mule to defend 'Uthman. Al-Ashtar met us and struck the mule in the face. She said, ‘Take me back, lest he disgrace me.’” He said: “Then she stationed Hasan between her residence and 'Uthman's residence, and she used to convey food and water to 'Uthman.”

names.arabic: إسحاق بن عبد اللَّه بن الحارث بن مسلم بن صفوان
names.english: Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Muslim ibn Safwan

unresolved.explanation: The canonical form is unvocalized. The Urdu witness preserves the same consonantal form, while the collateral Arabic works give conflicting spellings and do not establish its pronunciation. Sa'na is retained as the conservative provisional form.

The canonical word denotes a roofed structure and is rendered “roofed platform,” but the evidence does not establish its precise architectural form. The Urdu witness’s divergent “leather” cannot override the canonical Arabic.
